passages.title: Cooler blocks, block by block
passages.body:
On hot summer afternoons, downtown neighbourhoods with miles of concrete and asphalt can feel several degrees warmer than leafy suburbs. Scientists call this the urban heat-island effect: dark, paved surfaces soak up sunshine and release it slowly, while tailpipes and air conditioners add extra warmth to the air.

Last spring, the City of Mayfield launched a "Cool Blocks" pilot on three streets. Planners replaced some parking lanes with planters, added young trees protected by guards, and opened hose bib stations so residents could water new plantings on a shared schedule. A short handbook explained which hours were best for watering and how to spot drooping leaves before they browned.

Not everyone was convinced at first. Shop owners worried about fewer parking spots. Teen volunteers from the high school eco-club staffed weekend events, handed out door hangers, and painted cheerful murals on the new planters so the changes felt like a community project rather than a top-down rule. By August, merchants reported that shaded sidewalks drew more foot traffic during heat waves.

City staff cautioned that one pilot cannot erase the heat island by itself. Neighbouring blocks still radiate warmth, and small trees need years to cast wide shade. Still, organizers framed the programme as a practical first step: many hands keeping new roots alive, and data loggers measuring evening temperatures to see whether the coolest hours last a little longer than before.

questions.prompt: Which choice best states the central idea of the passage?
choices: Mayfield banned all cars from downtown streets
A neighbourhood pilot combined tree planting, shared watering, and outreach to reduce local heat stress
Scientists discovered that suburbs are always hotter than cities
Shop owners refused to participate in city programmes
questions.answer: A neighbourhood pilot combined tree planting, shared watering, and outreach to reduce local heat stress

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which factor contributes to the urban heat-island effect?
choices: dark paved surfaces absorbing and slowly releasing solar energy
trees that lose their leaves every winter
people walking instead of driving
rainfall washing dust off roads
questions.answer: dark paved surfaces absorbing and slowly releasing solar energy

questions.prompt: The eco-club’s murals and door hangers mainly served —
choices: to replace scientific measurements with art
to hide wilting plants from inspectors
to make street changes feel communal and welcoming
to advertise parking restrictions across the province
questions.answer: to make street changes feel communal and welcoming

questions.prompt: Which detail from the passage supports the idea that merchants eventually saw value in the pilot?
choices: They closed their shops during heat waves
They reported busier sidewalks when shade made walking more pleasant
They demanded that all students join the eco-club
They removed the hose bib stations
questions.answer: They reported busier sidewalks when shade made walking more pleasant

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention "data loggers" near the end?
choices: To show that volunteers replaced professional meteorologists
To signal that the city will ignore temperature readings
To explain how organisers plan to check whether nights cool off a bit more on pilot streets
To prove tree guards generate electricity
questions.answer: To explain how organisers plan to check whether nights cool off a bit more on pilot streets

questions.prompt: The watering handbook most likely aimed to —
choices: coordinate community care so new trees survive early dry spells
discourage residents from touching hose bib stations
require merchants to paint identical murals on every window
replace climate scientists with volunteers
questions.answer: coordinate community care so new trees survive early dry spells

questions.prompt: You can infer that some shop owners at first feared the pilot would —
choices: discourage customers who rely on nearby parking
force every building to install solar panels
eliminate all street trees in Mayfield
cancel summer school classes
questions.answer: discourage customers who rely on nearby parking

questions.prompt: Compared with the opening paragraph, the tone of the final paragraph is —
choices: more cautious about limits as well as hopeful about gradual progress
angry that suburbs refused to help
sarcastic about climate science
indifferent toward neighbourhood volunteers
questions.answer: more cautious about limits as well as hopeful about gradual progress

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, a "practical first step" implies the pilot is —
choices: the only action cities may ever take
a modest beginning that could lead to larger efforts if it succeeds
an impractical idea copied from fiction
a secret trial with no public benefits
questions.answer: a modest beginning that could lead to larger efforts if it succeeds

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows city staff avoiding the claim that the pilot fixes the entire city’s heat problem?
choices: Teen volunteers from the high school eco-club staffed weekend events
City staff cautioned that one pilot cannot erase the heat island by itself
Planners replaced some parking lanes with planters
A short handbook explained which hours were best for watering
questions.answer: City staff cautioned that one pilot cannot erase the heat island by itself
